limits: Completed throughput at fixed 200 DNS qps or 100 DHCP operations/s is not maximum capacity.
DNS latency uses formal-origin queries including late replies; window throughput excludes late completions.
DNS service CPU includes warmup and formal successful operations plus surrounding drain; dependencies are separate.
150-client DHCP CPU covers 150 DORA plus 2350 renewals; home6 covers six DORA plus 2494 renewals. These scales are separate and neither CPU interval is pure renewal.
Lifecycle child CPU is whole-round usage including startup, idle and teardown, not signal-only work. Readiness snapshots are not continuous peaks.
Formal resources select snapshots by their recorded timestamps; snapshots are non-atomic and all peaks are sampled peaks.
Helper sampled CPU excludes unsampled startup/teardown; complete lifetime receipts have a different scope.
PSS/USS unavailable; RssAnon and RSS cannot be called private physical memory. C tree RSS can duplicate shared pages.

Classification requires four of five paired directions and median relative delta above W; CPU also needs ten ticks every window and median delta above eight ticks. Lifecycle latency differences below one ms are not ranked.
Each formal window has fewer than ten thousand requests; no p99 is reported.
Loopback excludes Wi-Fi/Ethernet client path, real upstream latency, production hooks/ubus and address-conflict probing. Product code and production dnsmasq remain unchanged.
